correctness_confidence.basis: I re-derived by hand the constants in Theorem 1 (from (25)-(28), Lemma 15 and (27)), the Remark 9 constant (8/3)log17, the arithmetic in the proof of (3), the Jensen step, and the scaling and constant sqrt15/4^{4/3} in Prop. 14 given (22)-(23); all are consistent. I did not verify the Mathieu-based lower bound 1/sqrt8 of Thm 5, the Lemma 12 cone argument, the Theorem 13 parameter formulas (D, T, the explicit L,U,X,Y solution), or the uniformity claims, which are only sketched. No error found, but this is not full verification.

rigor.basis: The finite certificate (Lemmas 6-7, Prop. 8) and the Theorem 1 / Prop. 18 proofs are explicit and checkable. The superalgebraic and one-root constructions (Sec. 6, Thm 13) compress many uniformity steps (implicit-function dependence on R, Gaussian domination, outer-arc bounds, 'for some fixed kappa') into prose. Existential, non-quantitative thresholds are stated honestly. The Lemma 12 existence proof is terse.

novelty.basis: Novelty is incremental and relative to the cited arXiv:2608.02043 (Tan-Wang-Huang-Chen) and arXiv:2607.22017: removal of the log n factor in the exponent, exact threshold for interior-zero counts, a sharp circle-root limit 1/sqrt8, and a one-root n^{-1/6} construction. The paper discloses that the tools are classical and that the Erdos 973 negative answer was already known. I did not browse and could not verify the cited 2026 sources or search for antecedents; novelty is taken from the manuscript's own attributions.

significance.basis: A clean, narrow classification of when polynomial differentiation residuals can be superalgebraically small under zero-location constraints, with a sharp circle-root constant. It is of interest to the niche of Schur-stable polynomial residual bounds, but it does not resolve a major open problem; the paper itself leaves the optimal rate for one interior root (exponents 1/6 vs 13/6) and fixed-budget rates open.

reproducibility.basis: Constants and parameter formulas are explicit and checkable by the reader, and Section 9 describes exact and numerical diagnostics and states their limits (not interval-certified). No code or data is included in the PDF, and I executed nothing, so I cannot confirm that the described diagnostics were run or what they showed.

summary: The manuscript studies the infimum of ||P'-lambda P||_2/||P||_2 over degree-n polynomials with zeros in the closed disk, as a function of the number M of interior zeros. Main claims: (i) a finite-M lower bound (Thm 1) via a reciprocal identity, Mahler-type multiplication estimates and a Jensen estimate on a semicircle; (ii) an exact criterion that superalgebraic residual decay is possible iff the budget b_n tends to infinity (Thm 2, via the upper construction of Thm 4); (iii) a universal exp(-C sqrt n) lower bound with C > sqrt((8/3)log17), explicit exp(-3 sqrt n) for n >= 10^4 (Thm 3), built on a finite certificate; (iv) a sharp limit 1/sqrt8 for circle-only zeros (Thm 5); (v) one interior zero already gives O(n^{-1/6}) with an explicit family constant (Thm 13, Prop. 14) and a universal n^{-13/6} lower bound (Prop. 18); (vi) a polynomial barrier for a fixed root radius (Prop. 19). The paper is candid about non-optimality, non-quantitative thresholds, and its reliance on prior work. In the parts I re-derived (Thm 1 constants, Remark 9, Prop. 14 scaling, the arithmetic of (3)) I found no error; the heavy analytic constructions and the Mathieu bound are only sketched and I did not fully verify them. I did not browse or run code. Overall a competent, honest, incremental technical contribution.
strengths: Theorem 1 gives a fully explicit, all-degree lower bound whose proof is short and checkable (reciprocal identity, Poisson-kernel positivity, restricted-arc Jensen, Lemma 15).
The finite certificate (Prop. 8) turns an asymptotic claim into explicit parameter conditions, with a concrete threshold n >= 10^4 for exp(-3 sqrt n).
Theorem 2 gives a sharp characterization (b_n -> infinity) combining an upper construction with the Theorem 1 obstruction.
Careful and honest scoping: non-sharpness, existential thresholds, prior results and the limits of numerical checks are all stated explicitly.
weaknesses: The upper constructions (Thm 4, Thm 13, Lemma 12) are proved by compressed sketches; uniformity in n, k and the implicit-function step are asserted rather than fully quantified, so independent verification is hard.
Large gaps remain: 1/6 vs 13/6 for one interior zero, exp(-C sqrt n) vs superalgebraic bounds, and no quantitative M_A, C_A, N_A.
Novelty is relative to two very recent arXiv preprints and could not be independently checked here.

The numerical diagnostics are described but not included in the PDF, and the paper says they are not certified; the Mathieu-expansion step in Thm 5 relies on an asymptotic expansion used uniformly with only brief justification.
potential_errors: Thm 5 lower bound: the uniform-in-lambda use of the Mathieu asymptotic E(L) = -L + sqrt(L/2) - 1/16 + O(L^{-1/2}) on the window lambda = n/2 + O(sqrt n) and the odd-degree antiperiodic case are only briefly justified; the exact limit 1/sqrt8 depends on this. Possible gap, not shown to be an error.
Lemma 12: the passage from 'dual cone is zero' to 'finite union of columns generates R^{K-1}' and the rational strictly positive kernel vector is terse; plausible but unverified.
Thm 13: the explicit solution of D(a,c) = d_n, T(a,c) = t_n and the claim that the 34 residue classes of n are handled uniformly were not re-computed by me.
